metadata.summary: DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has confirmed that the plan is to keep the season-ending Play-offs in the Middle East, despite ongoing conflict in the region.
metadata.content: DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings confirms plan to stage Play-offs in Middle East, despite player safety concerns | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings confirms plan to stage Play-offs in Middle East, despite player safety concerns In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports, DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings discussed the plans for the season-ending Play-offs, the Strategic Alliance with the PGA Tour and the bright future the tour has within the global game By Ali Stafford at Wentworth Sunday 20 September 2026 15:01, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Matt Fitzpatrick voices his concerns over the DP World Tour Play-offs in the Middle East DP World Tour chief executive Guy Kinnings has confirmed that the plan is to keep the season-ending Play-offs in the Middle East, despite ongoing conflict in the region. The Abu Dhabi Championship is scheduled to be held at Yas Links on November 5-8, before the Race to Dubai season reaches its climax at the DP World Tour Championship the following week. There has been speculation throughout the season over whether both events would move to a different country, with Formula 1 cancelling two events earlier in the year in the region and discussions ongoing over whether races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead. messages.text: Great Britain book place in Davis Cup Finals with victory over Ecuador

metadata.summary: Great Britain wrapped up a straightforward victory over Ecuador to book their place at the Davis Cup Finals in November.
metadata.content: Davis Cup: Great Britain book place in Finals as Neal Skupski and Henry Patten victory over Ecuador | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Davis Cup: Great Britain book place in Finals as Neal Skupski and Henry Patten victory over Ecuador Neal Skupski and Henry Patten sealed Great Britain's place in the Davis Cup Finals in November, with a 6-3 6-4 win over Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo; it follows wins for Arthur Fery and Toby Samuel on Saturday, and means GB have reached the last eight for the first time since 2023 Stuart Hodge @Hodgeythehack Sunday 20 September 2026 14:51, UK Image: Great Britain's Henry Patten (left) and Neal Skupski celebrate during their match against Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo Great Britain wrapped up a straightforward victory over Ecuador to book their place at the Davis Cup Finals in November. After singles victories for Arthur Fery and Toby Samuel on Saturday at London's Copper Box, Henry Patten and Neal Skupski clinched the tie at the earliest opportunity with a 6-3 6-4 win against Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo in the doubles rubber. Britain therefore join three-time defending champions Italy, Canada, Czech Republic, South Korea and Austria in booking their spot for the eight-team event in Bologna. metadata.summary: "This is who we are. This is our team. This is City."
metadata.content: Gianluigi Donnarumma interview: Man City goalkeeper insists club are not in a transition year and backs club to have a great season | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Gianluigi Donnarumma interview: Man City goalkeeper insists club are not in a transition year and backs club to have a great season Man City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma speaks exclusively to Sky Sports' Sam Blitz about the club's faultless start to the campaign; after a summer of change, City have started on fire; watch Man City vs Sunderland live on Sky Sports this Sunday from 1pm, kick-off 2pm Sam Blitz Football Journalist @SamBIitz Sunday 20 September 2026 14:21, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma hails the performance of his team-mates after their 1-0 win at Manchester United at the weekend and says that VAR controversies are part of the game. "This is who we are. This is our team. This is City." It's been a few days since the Manchester Derby victory but sat at Man City's training ground, Gianluigi Donnarumma is still basking in the glory. He's not interested in Erling Haaland's controversial winner - though he's still annoyed Phil Foden was "harshly" sent off earlier in the game - as something else pleased him.
